qualification.reason: The document is an Expression of Interest (EOI) issued by the Ohio Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services for Recovery Month Events funding. It invites eligible organizations to apply for up to $10,000 to host activities, includes submission deadlines, eligibility requirements, and allowable expenses, making it a valid procurement opportunity.

quotes.quote: Recovery Month Events – Expression of Interest (EOI)
Request for Applications Due Date: 07/25/2025, by 3 p.m. EDT

OhioMHAS is requesting expressions of interest from potential prevention, treatment, and/or recovery supports providers; community coalitions; recovery community organizations; peer run organizations; housing providers; faith-based organizations; schools; and other non-profit community organizations.
Each eligible organization may request up to $10,000 to plan and implement activities and event(s)
Funding will be provided to organizations on a first-come, first-served basis.
All awards must be fully expended by September 29, 2025.
Please complete and submit the “Request for Funding Form” using the following link:

findings.title: Funding Disbursement via OhioPro
findings.fact: Organizations will be able to access the full amount of awarded funds once disbursement requirements are met. Awarded funds will be disbursed, via pass through agent, OhioPro.

quotes.quote: Organizations will be able to access the full amount of awarded funds once disbursement requirements are met. Awarded funds will be disbursed, via pass through agent, OhioPro.

findings.title: Reporting Requirement
findings.fact: Organizations are required to report to OhioMHAS how funds were utilized using the OhioMHAS outcomes survey. Completed surveys are due no later than November 7, 2025.

quotes.quote: Organizations are required to report to OhioMHAS how funds were utilized using the OhioMHAS outcomes survey. OhioMHAS will provide the survey link and the SOS questionnaire (if applicable) for required reporting. Completed surveys are due no later than November 7, 2025.

findings.title: Eligible Organization Types
findings.fact: Eligible organizations include prevention, treatment, and/or recovery supports providers; community coalitions; recovery community organizations; peer run organizations; housing providers; faith-based organizations; schools; and other non-profit community organizations.
findings.business_implication: This opportunity is open to a wide range of community-based organizations, not just traditional treatment providers. This expands the potential applicant pool and allows diverse entities to access funding for recovery events.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your organization falls within one of the listed categories. If you are a non-profit community organization, ensure you meet the definition and prepare to demonstrate your eligibility in the application.

quotes.quote: OhioMHAS is requesting expressions of interest from potential prevention, treatment, and/or recovery supports providers; community coalitions; recovery community organizations; peer run organizations; housing providers; faith-based organizations; schools; and other non-profit community organizations.

findings.title: Federal Tax Identification Number Required
findings.fact: Organizations must have a federal tax identification number (FTID).
findings.business_implication: Possession of a valid FTID is a mandatory prerequisite for eligibility. Without it, an organization cannot apply, regardless of its mission or capacity.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your organization has a valid FTID. If not, obtain one immediately. Ensure the FTID is correctly entered in the application form.

quotes.quote: Organizations must have a federal tax identification number (FTID).

findings.title: 501(c)(3) Non-Profit Requirement
findings.business_implication: Only organizations with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status are eligible. This restricts participation to non-profits and may exclude for-profit entities or those without formal non-profit status.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm your organization's 501(c)(3) status and have your IRS determination letter ready. If you are not yet 501(c)(3), consider partnering with a fiscal sponsor that is.

findings.title: Funding Expended by September 29, 2025
findings.fact: All awards must be fully expended by September 29, 2025.
findings.business_implication: The funding period is very short (approximately two months from award to expenditure deadline). This requires rapid planning and execution of events, and may limit the scope of activities that can be completed in time.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a detailed project plan with a tight timeline. Ensure that all planned events and activities can be completed and funds spent by September 29, 2025. Consider pre-planning and vendor contracts to expedite execution.

quotes.quote: All awards must be fully expended by September 29, 2025.

findings.title: EOI Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Expressions of interest must be submitted via the Microsoft form by July 25th at 3:00 p.m. EDT.
findings.business_implication: The deadline is firm and non-negotiable. Missing it will result in disqualification. The submission window is short (about two weeks from posting), so timely preparation is critical.
findings.action_recommendation: Mark the deadline on your calendar and aim to submit well before July 25th at 3:00 p.m. EDT. Prepare all required information in advance and test the Microsoft form to avoid technical issues.

quotes.quote: Request for Applications Due Date: 07/25/2025, by 3 p.m. EDT
